title: Four at the Teeth

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The cord knows what the mouth will not say, and the mouth knows what the cord will not count. Keep the two apart. Laying them together is a trade no honest house makes.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Weir, told sideways

where: Low Kiln, the Weir and Sill
pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-thirty-two-to-one-hundred-and-thirty-four-day-old body carried everywhere; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (the carrying arm as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, the finger beneath the board as a second account kept where nobody thinks to look, a sentence stopped at the word as an object on the interval tray, green at a mouth as a colour on its own place) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room, back-room interior, Ulda on stage, Fenna named in narration, present-tense break or ending

scenes.title: What the Arm Remembers
scenes.synopsis: First entry and first dated heading of Day 132, Reed 13, Thirdday, morning through midday at the Clay Yard and the reed beds. Sella Vail carries the boy at the half-pace from every open slate, gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, and goes around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the space under the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates and the empty place in the strip where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried, not paid). The reed bundles come in armfuls judged by the arm that carries them and by nothing set on a slate; a cutter tells a girl with a creel to lift it and let her arm tell her what went into it, and a man who asks what the work will want is given the weather and the river, never a figure (T071/T072, T077, T058/T079). The boy reads the carrying arm as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, exact and worth nothing. One hundred and thirty-two days old, four months and twelve days, he is told by nobody. Advances T071/T072, T077, T058/T079, T009/T013/T092, T098, T060/T086. Withheld: no figure for the reeds, no name, cause, body or count for the missing hand, no joining of the empty places.

scenes.title: A Finger Under the Board
scenes.synopsis: Second entry continued, Day 132, midday under the Vail kiln-house roof at the loaf shelf and the hearth. Sella sets the basket low at the angle at which the underside of the board becomes a roof and goes to the fire, telling it it was the thaw and giving the instruction to the pot and the broom and never to the basket (T058/T079). Above, the row keeps its two unnamed gaps, the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6 with no scrape, crumb, print or word, in a room the fold does not touch (T060/T086, T097 carried and unpaid). Standing with her back to the basket, moving her lips along the row, she reaches a finger BENEATH the board where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word, and takes it away; the boy sees the hand go under and come back and sees nothing of what the marks say. T100 is carried, not paid: he does not read, count, copy or join the strokes, does not lay the underside beside the two gaps above or the one stiff crust in the fold, and makes no cause of the habit (T100, T097). A neighbour come up from the strips with mud in her wrists asks what the row will want before the tend is out and is sent to the pot with the house has said it (T077). Advances T100 (carried), T060/T086, T097, T058/T079, T077. Withheld hard: no stroke counted, no figure read, no hand that copies the marks, no joining to the two gaps or any other absence.

scenes.title: The Cord Inside the Coat
scenes.synopsis: Third entry continued, Day 132, afternoon downriver at the Weir, the plank walk and flat blessing stone, then the going of the light and the small hours under the Vail roof. The reed work goes on in armfuls judged by the arm that carries them (T071/T072). The reed-cutter comes along the boards with a bundle and the short grey wool or reed-fibre cord gone grey with the oil of a working thumb; he sets the bundle on the flat stone, straightens the cord, turns it once so the knots stand, ties one low with his teeth and a thumb, bites the end off and puts it back inside his coat. To the woman who asks what the cord holds he says You can ask the cord and No more can the Court; no figure, knot, name or joining (T099 carried, not paid). Orra Weir stands at the lower boards with her board on its side and pulls one knot down, giving a date where a levy question was asked earlier and keeping the word forty unspoken with the forty-first double turn legible and unnamed (T024/T059/T025). Mira Silt works the eels, answers a thin run with her own answer, moves eel-bones while deciding whether to lie and puts her thumb under her apron to the grey cord when a buyer names a figure; the second twist twisted twice stays beneath it, never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted (T059/T025/T024). At dusk Sella sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen, tells the fire it was the thaw and says The house will keep it; the river's note, the carried fire's missing fifth breath with its payer unnamed for a hundred and thirty-two days and the boards' four nails, four and a knot keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T088, T071/T072). Advances T099, T024/T059/T025, T088, T071/T072, T058/T079.

scenes.title: The Dust Ahead of the Fire
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry and first dated heading of Day 133, Reed 14, Fourthday, before first grey through midday at the Vail wheel-shed, its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the cold damper and the Clay Yard. Three or four unnamed men come up with their collars high and speak low in the room off the shed; Sella carries the boy past at the half-pace, gives the house no name for them and does not say the room was cold (T035/T031). Jorra Vail comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger, not bone-coloured slip, keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate; he speaks to the wheel before anyone (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady), tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note before it leaves the wheel and withholds the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master who would call it early and make something of it (T035/T031/T062). Before Sella has finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper, moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves it standing, and the household straightens around his silence. The boy reads the iron again as the bite that holds a vessel whole and the bite that can take the hand off a man, with no Grathic word for both mercies, and files it as an object worth nothing joined to no kiln (T062); the two tellings of the shut room stay beside it with no third telling (T065/T095). Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late and wants the late because it puts off the paying; his seventh year is pressed past another tend and still held, the knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the breath from Seed 16 unspent (T036/T076). His stroke goes on over the flagstones without the half-check while the stones keep the shallow bright patch where it stopped; neither man names the other's silence and the broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, entered by nobody (T031, T036/T076). Advances T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T036/T076, T058/T079, T009/T013/T092. Withheld: no name for the men, no third telling, no calling of the loan, no spending of the seventh year.

scenes.title: The Fourth Stopping
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry continued, Day 133, late afternoon at the out-of-line landing below the north bridge and the going of the light into the small hours at the hearth and kindling under the Vail roof. The soft-cuffed clerk is still set at the landing for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, slate to his forearm and hand to slate before eyes to stalls; the market sells its reeds and eels over the top of him, nobody steps around him and nobody takes him off (T090/T080/T083). At the hearth, with coals banked and the small knife set back where it can be checked, Tarn tells the kindling Six counted. The next I don't count, and then the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes a FOURTH time all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name (T036/T076). He draws the breath that should go in at the top of the reach and does not spend it, says Yes, house to the fire and goes on with the broom. Sella, within hearing, gives the end of her instruction to the pot and asks nothing; Jorra does not ask about the ear and Tarn does not ask about the room, and the two silences stay unjoined. The chapter's one meaningful change: the boy files the fourth stopping on the interval tray beside the first three as a FOURTH INTERVAL AND NOT A FOURTH PAYMENT, an object among objects and not a rule, refusing to let four stoppings stand up and call themselves a doctrine; the loan stays uncalled and the seventh year has still not given (T036/T076, T061/T082). The carried fire keeps its four low pulls and its silent fifth with its payer unnamed for a hundred and thirty-three days (T088). Advances T036/T076 (fourth stopping withheld), T061/T082, T090/T080/T083, T088, T058/T079. Withheld: no calling word spoken, no figure, no name, no payment, no seventh hearing.

scenes.title: Four Greens and a Cold Foot
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry and first dated heading of Day 134, Reed 15, Fifthday, morning at the Cross, the market stalls and the pot board, then below the sill at the fish-trade shade. A silent woman stands across the square with the sweetish lead-glaze green at one corner of her mouth, clay under her nails and a pale line across the back of one hand where something was once worn tight and long enough to leave its mark; she turns a cup a quarter on the board, sets it back where it stood and goes off with the light, unnamed and silent. This is the FOURTH green at a mouth and the FIVE shapes of the colour counting Berr Clay's glaze at his own mouth, filed beside the Silt 30, Seed 28 and Reed 7 greens on places that do not touch --- a colour and not a name, never Fenna in the narration (T050/T051). Berr comes up short with the red office cord folded under his coat, wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, buys eels two marks short and says a number goes into a slate, not a bundle, taking himself out of his own sentence with your house, never I; his green stays on its own place and is not joined to the woman's (T015/T041/T047, T050/T051). Mira answers a question about the run with her own answer, moves eel-bones while deciding whether to lie and shows the second cord twisted twice beneath the grey with neither knot counted, her board beside Orra Weir's and not touching (T059/T025/T024). Below the sill a child's foot stays dark inside three turns of wool, the cold to the woman who wrapped it and weather to the yard; the surgeon's reading of the extremity going before the core works and buys nothing, and no silt-leach, cause, cure or recognition is written across it (T093/T094/T096). Advances T050/T051 (fourth green), T015/T041/T047, T059/T025/T024, T093/T094/T096, T090/T080. Withheld: the woman is not named or given dialogue and is not Fenna in narration, no ear is spoken with the colour, no knot counted, no word forty, no silt-leach or cure named.

scenes.title: One Hundred and Thirty-Four
scenes.synopsis: Seventh entry continued, Day 134, afternoon under the Vail kiln-house roof, the loaf shelf and then the going of the light into the small hours on the bed. Sella stands at the shelf with her back to the basket, moves her lips along the row with its two unnamed gaps, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and reaches a finger beneath the board where the charcoal tally lies without looking and without a word, then takes the finger away, unexplained (T100 carried, not paid; T058/T079). At dusk she carries him up the clay road at the half-pace, goes around the space beneath the lowest rack, sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen, her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting before it goes away; she tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, sets the pot rim out and handle toward the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079). He turns out his file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds every object in its place and nothing joined: six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh, the told bell beside the heard bell, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, the intervals with the FOUR stoppings as objects and not a rule, the damper's double bite filed joined to no kiln, the two shut-room tellings with no third, one crust in the fold with its empty place unnamed and no third, the two shelf gaps in a room that does not touch, the charcoal under the shelf on a place of its own, the word forty unspoken with the readable double turn beside it, the cold foot still the cold to one woman and weather to the yard, Alda's six pages and both tins and Dessa's pewter tin shut, the clerk still set, the loan uncalled and the seventh year not given (T061/T082, T036/T076, T060/T086, T100, T023/T089, T090/T080, T093/T094/T096, T097). Through the finger's-width door comes the river's note, through the floor the carried fire's missing fifth breath with its payer unnamed for a hundred and thirty-four days, overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a knot: three counts in three places that do not become one (T088, T071/T072). One hundred and thirty-four days old, four months and fourteen days, he is told by nobody; the hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down with the count exact, unspent and spoken by nobody. Advances T061/T082, T036/T076, T060/T086, T100, T088, T071/T072, T097. Nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called or ended; forward, not closed.
